reasoning: Patient is alert and oriented with stable presentation; no immediate life threat → not ESI-1
Chief complaint is localized eye trauma (foreign body) with pain and tearing; vital signs reported as normal limits → not ESI-2 (no high-risk presentation, severe distress, or altered mental status)

Foreign body in eye requires multiple resources: visual inspection/slit lamp exam, possible imaging (CT if penetrating injury suspected), irrigation/removal procedure, ophthalmology evaluation or referral, topical anesthetics, antibiotics, discharge instructions

Mechanism (chainsaw without eye protection) raises concern for potential penetrating injury or significant corneal abrasion despite benign-sounding history; cannot rule out serious injury at triage without examination
Young, healthy adult with no comorbidities reduces risk of atypical presentation
Meets ESI-3 criteria: stable vitals, alert, requires multiple diagnostic/treatment resources (exam, potential imaging, procedure, specialist evaluation)
red_flags: High-velocity mechanism (chainsaw) — potential for penetrating globe injury or intraocular foreign body not apparent on surface inspection
Vitals not yet recorded — should be obtained immediately to confirm stability
Inability to fully assess visual acuity, pupil reactivity, or anterior chamber integrity at triage without equipment
Risk of vision-threatening delay if deeper ocular injury (hyphema, retinal detachment, iridodialysis) is present
